text:
Scrounging through woodland leaf litter, tormull ravenously pull rotten wood and mulched leaves into their grinding mandibles. Like 
its distant relative, the bloomux, the insect will fi ll its abdomen to near bursting for the need of its spawn. When fi lled, with its thorned, 
swollen abdomen dragging along the ground, it will lumber back into the subterranean pits to regurgitate the plant-matter. Not for 
their larvae, but for the multitude of luminescent fungal clusters that cover the lair walls, which the larvae swarm over hungrily, nearly 
obscuring the blue glowing fungus with their black shelled bodies. Once grown past their larval form, they enter a phase of abrupt 
cannibalism, leaving only a few of the ravenous aphids to ever reach their adult size and continue the cycle of fungal farming.
